figures.evidence: Suppressed non-Maliki legal schools and burned books of other madhahib in Córdoba.

figures.name: Al-Muzani

figures.name: Al-Mutawakkil

figures.name: Al-Tabari
figures.evidence: Documented multiple juristic opinions in his works, preserving early legal disagreement.

figures.name: Ibn Surayj

figures.name: Sahl al-Su'luki

figures.name: Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini

figures.name: Al-Sarakhsi

figures.name: Al-Hajj Salim Suwari

figures.name: Ahmad Baba al-Timbukti

figures.name: Abdurauf Fitrat

figures.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi

figures.name: Abdurrahman Wahid

figures.name: Abdolkarim Soroush

books.evidence: Reflects modernist linguistic sensibility in reformist Quranic commentary.

books.title_ar: عبقري الإصلاح والتعليم: الإمام محمد عبده

concepts.definition_ar: مشروع القرن التاسع عشر والعشرين لتحديث المفردات العربية وتبسيط النحو.
concepts.definition_ur: انیسویں اور بیسویں صدی کا منصوبہ عربی الفاظ کو جدید بنانا اور نحو کو آسان کرنا۔

concepts.name: Al-Manzila bayn al-Manzilatayn (intermediate position)
concepts.definition: Mu'tazili doctrine that a grave sinner is neither a believer nor an unbeliever.

figures.name: Zayd ibn Ali
figures.evidence: Adopted Mu'tazili position on grave sinners in his theological framework.

figures.name: Al-Jubba'i
figures.evidence: Transmitted classical Mu'tazili position on grave sinners' intermediate status.

figures.name: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Ahmad
figures.evidence: Elaborated intermediate status of grave sinner in Sharḥ al-uṣūl al-khamsah.

concepts.definition_ar: عقيدة المعتزلة بأن مرتكب الكبيرة ليس مؤمناً ولا كافراً
concepts.definition_ur: معتزلی عقیدہ کہ کبیرہ گناہ کا مرتکب نہ مومن ہے نہ کافر

concepts.name: Iman (definition of faith)
concepts.definition: Whether faith is inward assent, verbal profession, works, or all three combined.

figures.name: Khadija bint Khuwaylid
figures.evidence: First person to profess faith combining assent and public profession of Islam.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
figures.evidence: Exemplified prophetic definition of faith through immediate acceptance of Muhammad's message.

figures.name: Amr ibn al-As
figures.evidence: Early Companion who transmitted foundational understanding of faith from the Prophet's era.

figures.name: Masruq ibn al-Ajda
figures.evidence: Known to transmit early views on faith from Companions like Umar and Ibn Masud.

figures.name: Hasan al-Basri
figures.evidence: His definitions of faith as including works influenced Kharijite and Murji'ite debates.

figures.name: Jabir ibn Zayd
figures.evidence: Articulated that faith requires both belief and works, foundational to Ibadi theology.

figures.name: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani
figures.evidence: As Tabi'i scholar in Basra, transmitted early community teachings on faith's definition.

figures.name: Imam Abu Hanifa
figures.evidence: Defined faith as recognition and affirmation in Al-Fiqh al-Akbar, influencing Maturidi theology.

figures.name: Sufyan al-Thawri
figures.evidence: As ascetic teacher, transmitted early pietist understanding of faith from Kufa.

figures.name: Waki ibn al-Jarrah
figures.evidence: Known work 'Zuhd' reflects early pious tradition on faith and ascetic practice.

figures.name: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
figures.evidence: Defined faith as statement, belief, and action in opposition to Murji'i minimalism.

figures.name: Imam al-Bukhari
figures.evidence: Sahih al-Bukhari includes Book of Faith defining iman through prophetic reports.

figures.name: Imam Muslim
figures.evidence: Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Iman transmits prophetic definitions of faith and its components.

figures.name: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
figures.evidence: Sahih Muslim contains the Book of Faith (Kitab al-Iman) transmitting hadith on faith's definition.

figures.name: Muhammad al-Tirmidhi
figures.evidence: Transmitted hadiths on the definition of faith in his Jami' al-Tirmidhi.

figures.name: Al-Tahawi
figures.evidence: Al-Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah defines faith as assent, profession, and works combined.

figures.name: Abu Mansur al-Maturidi
figures.evidence: Defined faith as tasdiq (assent) with works as completion not essence in Kitab al-Tawhid.

figures.name: Al-Maturidi
figures.evidence: Defined faith as conviction and affirmation, with works as perfection not essence.

figures.name: Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari
figures.evidence: Addressed definition of faith in Maqalat, mediating between Kharijite and Murji'ite extremes.

figures.name: Al-Ash'ari
figures.evidence: Treated faith as assent with verbal profession, allowing degrees, in Al-Ibana.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi
figures.evidence: Defends Sufi understanding of faith as compatible with Sunni orthodoxy in his work.

figures.name: Al-Baghawi
figures.evidence: Sharh al-Sunna preserves traditional Sunni definition of faith as creed and works.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Iman defines faith as belief, speech, and deed, increasing and decreasing.

figures.name: Ibn al-Qayyim
figures.evidence: Discusses faith as belief, speech, and action in Madarij al-Salikin.

figures.name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
figures.evidence: Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam systematically treats faith's definition through hadith commentary.

figures.name: Al-Laqqani
figures.evidence: Jawhara defines faith following Ash'ari understanding.

figures.name: Bediuzzaman Said Nursi
figures.evidence: Risale-i Nur systematically explores certainty levels and rational foundations of faith.

figures.name: Malcolm X
figures.evidence: Redefined faith to include social justice action in 'The Ballot or the Bullet' speech.

figures.name: Fethullah Gülen
figures.evidence: Discusses definition and components of faith in The Essentials of the Islamic Faith.

concepts.definition_ar: هل الإيمان تصديق بالقلب أم إقرار باللسان أم عمل أم جميعها
concepts.definition_ur: کیا ایمان دل کی تصدیق ہے یا زبان کا اقرار یا عمل یا سب

concepts.name: Wujud and Mahiyya (existence and essence)
concepts.definition: Whether existence is really distinct from essence in created things, and what that implies for God.

figures.name: Abu al-Hassan al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Al-Amiri's al-Amad ala al-Abad treats essence-existence distinction in creatures.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Extended Avicennan metaphysics in his philosophical treatise Miftah al-Tibb.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Systematized essence-existence distinction in Al-Shifa, treating existence as accident of essence.

figures.name: Al-Shahrastani
figures.evidence: Treats existence-essence distinction philosophically in Nihaya al-iqdam.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Treats existence-essence through light metaphysics, prioritizing light over quiddity.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Advanced Avicennan metaphysics of existence-essence distinction in Tajrid al-I'tiqad.

figures.name: Muhammad ibn Muhammad Tabrizi
figures.evidence: 13th-century Persian philosopher likely engaged Avicennan metaphysics standard in his era.

figures.name: Sadr al-Din al-Qunawi
figures.evidence: Integrated existence-essence distinction with mystical metaphysics in dialogue with philosophers.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Systematically treated existence-essence distinction in Hikmat al-Ishraq commentary.

figures.name: Allama Hilli
figures.evidence: Engaged Avicennan metaphysics in theological context following earlier Shia scholars.

figures.name: Dawud al-Kayseri
figures.evidence: Merged Avicennan metaphysics with Akbarian theosophy in his philosophical works.

figures.name: Al-Taftazani
figures.evidence: Transmitted Avicennan metaphysical distinctions in theological context.

figures.name: Al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Kitāb al-taʻrīfāt provides canonical definitions distinguishing existence and essence.

figures.name: Ali ibn Mohammed al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Jurjani Definitions (Kitāb al-taʻrīfāt) provides technical definitions of philosophical terms including essence.

figures.name: Molla Fenari
figures.evidence: Studied under Dawud al-Kayseri, key transmitter of Ibn Arabi's ontology to Ottoman realm.

figures.name: Sadr ad-Din Dashtaki
figures.evidence: Extended debates on existence-essence distinction in his commentaries on Ibn Sina and Tusi.

figures.name: Ibn Abi Jumhur al-Ahsa'i
figures.evidence: Combined Avicennan essence-existence with Illuminationist metaphysics in Mujli al-Ahzan.

figures.name: Mir Damad
figures.evidence: Developed theory of huduth dahri (perpetual origination) in Qabasat reconciling essence and existence.

figures.name: Mir Fendereski
figures.evidence: Engaged existence-essence distinction in his metaphysical works bridging traditions.

figures.name: Mulla Sadra
figures.evidence: Resolves existence-essence debate by prioritizing existence in Hikmat al-Muta'aliya.

figures.name: Rajab Ali Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Worked on existence-essence distinction as part of Sadrian philosophical tradition.

figures.name: Qazi Sa’id Qumi
figures.evidence: Qumi wrote extensively on existence-essence distinction in his philosophical commentaries.

figures.name: Abdu Al Rahim Damavandi
figures.evidence: Core metaphysical distinction taught in 18th-century Iranian philosophical curriculum.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Extensively treated existence-essence distinction in his Manzuma philosophical poem.

figures.name: Allameh Sayyed Abul Hasan Rafiee Qazvini
figures.evidence: As traditional Iranian philosopher, would have taught Avicennan distinction in Qazvin seminary.

figures.name: Mirza Mahdi Elahi Qomshehei
figures.evidence: As Isfahan school philosopher, likely engaged existence-essence debates central to that tradition.

figures.name: Muhammad Husayn Tabatabaei
figures.evidence: Developed existence-essence distinction following Mulla Sadra in philosophical works.

figures.name: Mohammad-Taqi Ja'fari
figures.evidence: Major contributions to ontological debates on existence-essence distinction in Islamic philosophy.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Engaged deeply with existence-essence distinction in his works on Islamic philosophy.

figures.name: Nasrollah Hekmat
figures.evidence: Contemporary Islamic philosopher in Tehran engaging foundational metaphysical distinctions.

figures.name: Ali Asghar Mosleh
figures.evidence: Active in Iranian philosophical debates on existence-essence distinction.

concepts.definition_ar: هل الوجود مغاير حقاً للماهية في الممكنات وما يترتب على ذلك في حق الله
concepts.definition_ur: کیا ممکنات میں وجود ماہیت سے حقیقتاً الگ ہے

concepts.name: Wajib and Mumkin (necessary and contingent being)
concepts.definition: Dividing all that exists into what must exist in itself and what might or might not.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Formulated necessary-contingent division and proof of God in Al-Najat and Al-Isharat.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Systematized necessary-contingent being distinction in Tajrid al-I'tiqad.

figures.name: Dawud al-Kayseri
figures.evidence: Integrated necessary-contingent distinction into Akbarian ontology.

figures.name: Al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Definitions text systematizes necessary versus contingent being distinction.

figures.name: Mir Damad
figures.evidence: Systematized necessary-contingent distinction in his metaphysics throughout al-Rawashih al-Samawiyya.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Refined necessary-contingent being analysis in his systematic philosophical works.

concepts.definition_ar: تقسيم الموجودات إلى ما يجب وجوده بذاته وما يجوز وجوده وعدمه
concepts.definition_ur: موجودات کی تقسیم واجب الوجود اور ممکن الوجود میں

concepts.name: Al-Aql al-Fa'al (Active Intellect)
concepts.definition: The cosmic intellect that actualizes human thought and grants prophetic knowledge.

figures.name: Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi
figures.evidence: Referenced cosmic intellect mediating celestial influences in his theory of astral causation.

figures.name: Al-Kindi
figures.evidence: On the Intellect first introduces Active Intellect doctrine into Arabic philosophy.

figures.name: Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi
figures.evidence: Integrated Active Intellect into Ismaili cosmology as source of prophetic knowledge.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Detailed Active Intellect as agent of human knowledge in epistemology and politics.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Discussed Active Intellect's role in illuminating human souls in al-Muntakhab Siwan al-Hikma.

figures.name: Al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Used Active Intellect theory in explaining prophetic knowledge and human intellection.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Developed Active Intellect as source of human intellection in De Anima of Al-Shifa.

figures.name: Mu'ayyad fi'l-Din al-Shirazi
figures.evidence: Discussed Active Intellect's role in cosmology throughout his philosophical treatises.

figures.name: Nasir Khusraw
figures.evidence: Integrates Active Intellect into Ismaili cosmology of universal intellect and soul.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Tadbir al-Mutawahhid develops theory of conjunction with Active Intellect for human perfection.

figures.name: Ibn Tufayl
figures.evidence: Hayy achieves union with Active Intellect as climax of rational ascent.

figures.name: Ibn Rushd
figures.evidence: Rejected Avicenna's separate Active Intellect in unity of the intellect treatise.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Recasts Active Intellect as Lord of Species in illuminationist cosmology.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Treated Active Intellect theory in his synthesis of peripatetic thought.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Discusses Active Intellect in philosophical commentaries following Avicenna.

concepts.definition_ar: العقل الكوني الذي يُفعّل الفكر الإنساني ويمنح المعرفة النبوية
concepts.definition_ur: وہ کونیاتی عقل جو انسانی فکر کو فعال کرتی ہے

concepts.name: Nafs Natiqa (the rational soul)
concepts.definition: The immaterial human soul in Avicennan philosophy, its faculties and survival after death.

figures.name: Abu Hatim Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Razi
figures.evidence: Transmitted Neoplatonic psychology of rational soul in Ismaili framework.

figures.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
figures.evidence: Translated and wrote 'The Difference between Spirit and Soul' on Galenic psychology.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Treated rational soul's faculties in his psychology, pre-Avicennan framework.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Explored rational soul's nature and immortality in his philosophical anthology.

figures.name: Al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Developed theory of rational soul in philosophical works on happiness and human perfection.

figures.name: Abu al-Hassan al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Treats rational soul's immortality in psychological works following Aristotle.

figures.name: Al-Tawhidi
figures.evidence: Discussed psychology of the rational soul extensively in al-Imta wa-l-Mu'anasa.

figures.name: Miskawayh
figures.evidence: Tahdhib al-Akhlaq analyzes rational soul's faculties and moral development.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Transmitted Avicennan psychology through his medical and philosophical works.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Refined rational soul theory and floating man argument for soul's independence in Al-Shifa.

figures.name: Mu'ayyad fi'l-Din al-Shirazi
figures.evidence: Transmitted Avicennan psychology within Isma'ili philosophical framework.

figures.name: Nasir Khusraw
figures.evidence: Discusses rational soul within Ismaili philosophical anthropology in prose works.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Risala fi al-Nafs details rational soul's ascent from material to intellectual actualization.

figures.name: Ibn Tufayl
figures.evidence: Hayy ibn Yaqzan traces soul's self-development from isolation to rational perfection.

figures.name: Ibn Rushd
figures.evidence: Challenged Avicennan individual soul immortality in unity of intellect works.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Treats rational soul through light ontology in Philosophy of Illumination.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Discussed rational soul doctrine in his philosophical encyclopedia.

figures.name: Sadr ad-Din Dashtaki
figures.evidence: Refined Avicennan psychology in his philosophical works on the rational soul.

figures.name: Mulla Sadra
figures.evidence: Treats soul's transubstantial motion in Kasr al-asnam al-jahiliyyah.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Covered Avicennan rational soul doctrine in his philosophical teaching.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Covered Avicennan psychology in his teaching of Islamic peripatetic philosophy.

concepts.definition_ar: النفس الإنسانية المجردة في الفلسفة الابن سينوية وقواها وبقاؤها بعد الموت
concepts.definition_ur: ابن سینا کی فلسفے میں مجرد انسانی روح اور اس کی قوتیں

concepts.name: Ishraq (illuminationism)
concepts.definition: Suhrawardi's philosophy of light as fundamental reality and knowledge as presence.

figures.name: Ibn Tufayl
figures.evidence: Hayy's mystical illumination echoes earlier illuminationist philosophical themes.

figures.name: Yahya Suhrawardi (Maqtul)
figures.evidence: Founded illuminationist philosophy in 'Philosophy of Illumination' (Hikmat al-Ishraq).

figures.name: Ibn Sab'in
figures.evidence: Known as Shaykh al-Ishraq al-Gharbi, reviving illuminationism in the West.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Al-Shahrazuri wrote extensive commentaries on Suhrawardi's illuminationist works.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Wrote major commentary on Suhrawardi's Hikmat al-Ishraq.

figures.name: Sadr ad-Din Dashtaki
figures.evidence: Transmitted Suhrawardi's illuminationist texts to his students in Shiraz school.

figures.name: Ibn Abi Jumhur al-Ahsa'i
figures.evidence: Merged Suhrawardi's Illuminationism with Peripatetic philosophy in his synthesis.

figures.name: Mir Damad
figures.evidence: Merged Suhrawardian illuminationist themes with Peripatetic metaphysics in Isfahan school.

figures.name: Mir Fendereski
figures.evidence: Merged Suhrawardi's illuminationism with Peripatetic philosophy in his philosophical system.

figures.name: Rajab Ali Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Combined illuminationist themes with Sadrian metaphysics in Isfahan tradition.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Integrated illuminationist elements with Sadraean philosophy in his synthesis.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Taught Suhrawardi's illuminationist philosophy alongside Sadrian thought.

figures.name: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
figures.evidence: Discusses Suhrawardi's illuminationism extensively in Three Muslim Sages.

figures.name: Nasrollah Pourjavady
figures.evidence: As Tehran philosophy scholar, translates illuminationist texts into Persian context.

figures.name: Nasrollah Hekmat
figures.evidence: Iranian philosopher likely exposed to Suhrawardian illuminationist currents in Tehran.

concepts.definition_ar: فلسفة السهروردي في النور كحقيقة أساسية والمعرفة كحضور
concepts.definition_ur: سہروردی کا فلسفہ نور بطور بنیادی حقیقت اور معرفت بطور حضور

concepts.name: Mantiq (logic)
concepts.definition: The Aristotelian syllogistic apparatus naturalized into Islamic scholarly curricula.

figures.name: Ibn al-Muqaffa
figures.evidence: Translated Persian works incorporating Aristotelian logic into Arabic intellectual culture.

figures.name: Ma'mun al-Rashid
figures.evidence: Sponsored translation of Aristotle's Organon into Arabic at Bayt al-Hikma.

figures.name: Al-Kindi
figures.evidence: Die philosophischen Abhandlungen transmits Aristotelian logic to Arabic scholarship.

figures.name: Hunayn ibn Ishaq
figures.evidence: Translated Aristotle's Organon and Porphyry's Isagoge, making Greek logic available in Arabic.

figures.name: Qusta ibn Luqa
figures.evidence: Translated Aristotelian logical works as part of Greek-Arabic translation movement.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Wrote extensive commentaries on Aristotle's Organon, naturalized logic into Islamic curriculum.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Preserved and transmitted Aristotelian logic in Baghdad philosophical circle's curriculum.

figures.name: Al-Tawhidi
figures.evidence: Engaged Aristotelian logic in al-Muqabasat and debates with Abu Sulayman al-Sijistani.

figures.name: Ibn al-Nadim
figures.evidence: Al-Fihrist catalogues logical works and translators of Greek logic into Arabic.

figures.name: Abū Hayyān al-Tawhīdī
figures.evidence: Studied logic under Yahya ibn Adi, a leading Aristotelian logician of Baghdad.

figures.name: Ibn Hindu
figures.evidence: Systematized Aristotelian logic in works taught to later Persian scholars.

figures.name: Ibn Sina
figures.evidence: Systematized Aristotelian logic in Al-Shifa and Al-Isharat for Islamic philosophy curriculum.

figures.name: Ibn al-Sīd al-Baṭalyawsī
figures.evidence: As Andalusian philosopher trained in falsafa tradition, engaged Aristotelian logical methods.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Mantiq transmits Aristotelian logic to Andalusian philosophical tradition.

figures.name: Fakhr al-Din Razi
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Mulahhas fi l-hikma wal-mantiq transmits Aristotelian logic systematically.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Commentary on Avicenna's Isharat transmitted Peripatetic logic to later generations.

figures.name: Al-Baydawi
figures.evidence: Tawali' al-Anwar employs Aristotelian logical methods in theological argumentation.

figures.name: Muhammad ibn Muhammad Tabrizi
figures.evidence: Aristotelian logic was core curriculum for Islamic philosophers in Tabriz by 13th century.

figures.name: Al-Shahrazuri
figures.evidence: Included logical treatises in his comprehensive philosophical works.

figures.name: Qutb al-Din Shirazi
figures.evidence: Treated Aristotelian logic in philosophical commentaries.

figures.name: Allama Hilli
figures.evidence: Employed Aristotelian logic systematically in theological argumentation and jurisprudence.

figures.name: Ibn Taymiyya
figures.evidence: Naqd al-Mantiq systematically refutes Aristotelian logic as unnecessary for Islamic sciences.

figures.name: Al-Idji
figures.evidence: Advanced logical theory in al-Risala al-Wad'iyya on linguistic conventions.

figures.name: Al-Taftazani
figures.evidence: Produced major commentaries on logic including works on Aristotelian syllogistics.

figures.name: Ibn Khaldun
figures.evidence: Muqaddimah incorporates Aristotelian logic in methodology of historical analysis.

figures.name: Al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Ḥāshiyat on Shamsīyah systematizes Aristotelian logic for Islamic curriculum.

figures.name: Ali ibn Mohammed al-Jurjani
figures.evidence: Ḥāshiyat ʻalá taṣawwurāt sharḥ al-Risālah al-shamsīyah fī al-qawāʻid al-manṭiqīyah is a commentary on logic.

figures.name: Molla Fenari
figures.evidence: Wrote glosses on logic texts, establishing Ottoman madrasa curriculum in Bursa.

figures.name: Ali Qushji
figures.evidence: Sharh al-Risalah al-Wadiyah treats Aristotelian logic for theological students.

figures.name: Mehmed II
figures.evidence: Studied philosophy under scholars like George Scholarius and established madrasas teaching logic.

figures.name: Qazi Sa’id Qumi
figures.evidence: Taught Aristotelian logic as part of standard philosophical curriculum in Qom.

figures.name: Gelenbevi Ismail Efendi
figures.evidence: Islamic sciences scholar in Ottoman tradition taught Aristotelian logic as standard curriculum.

figures.name: Al-Bajuri
figures.evidence: AuthoredHashiyaÊ» ala Sharh al-Sullam, a commentary on Akhdarī's logic text.

figures.name: Abbasgulu Bakikhanov
figures.evidence: As philosopher, likely engaged Aristotelian logic common in 19th-century curricula.

figures.name: Hadi Sabzavari
figures.evidence: Taught Aristotelian logic as foundation of his philosophical curriculum.

figures.name: Mohammad-Taqi Ja'fari
figures.evidence: Taught and transmitted Aristotelian logic within Islamic philosophical curriculum at Tabriz.

figures.name: Allama Seyyed jalal al-addin Ashtiani
figures.evidence: Taught traditional Aristotelian logic as part of philosophical training in Qom.

concepts.definition_ar: الجهاز القياسي الأرسطي الذي تبنّته المناهج العلمية الإسلامية
concepts.definition_ur: ارسطو کی قیاسی منطق جو اسلامی علمی نصاب میں شامل ہوئی

concepts.name: Sa'ada (philosophical happiness)
concepts.definition: The ultimate end of human life conceived as intellectual and moral perfection.

figures.name: Ibn al-Muqaffa
figures.evidence: Transmitted Persian philosophical ethics on virtuous life in his Adab al-Kabir.

figures.name: Al-Farabi
figures.evidence: Defined happiness as ultimate intellectual perfection in Tahsil al-Sa'ada.

figures.name: Al-Sijistani
figures.evidence: Discussed philosophical happiness as ultimate end in his ethical writings.

figures.name: Al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Central theme in his al-I'lam bi-Manaqib al-Islam, treating happiness as philosophical end.

figures.name: Abu al-Hassan al-Amiri
figures.evidence: Al-Sa'ada wa al-Is'ad synthesizes Aristotelian and Islamic views on ultimate happiness.

figures.name: Miskawayh
figures.evidence: Systematized virtue ethics in Tahdhib al-Akhlaq, defining happiness as soul perfection.

figures.name: Abū Hayyān al-Tawhīdī
figures.evidence: Discusses philosophical happiness and human fulfillment in his salon dialogues.

figures.name: Omar Khayyam
figures.evidence: Rubaiyat explores earthly pleasure and philosophical contentment as human fulfillment themes.

figures.name: Ibn Bajja
figures.evidence: Tadbir al-Mutawahhid presents solitary philosopher's path to intellectual happiness via contemplation.

figures.name: Nizami Ganjavi
figures.evidence: Khamsa integrates philosophical happiness with mystical love and ethical virtue.

figures.name: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Merged philosophical ethics with Persian tradition in Akhlaq-i Nasiri.

figures.name: Abbas el-Akkad
figures.evidence: Examined human excellence and genius through biographical studies of historical exemplars.

figures.name: Mohammed Aziz Lahbabi
figures.evidence: Reinterpreted philosophical happiness through personalist lens of authentic self-realization.

concepts.definition_ar: الغاية القصوى للحياة الإنسانية بوصفها كمالاً عقلياً وأخلاقياً
concepts.definition_ur: انسانی زندگی کا حتمی مقصد بطور عقلی اور اخلاقی کمال

concepts.name: Maslaha (public welfare)
concepts.definition: Using the common good as a criterion for legal rulings where texts are silent.

figures.name: Umar ibn al-Khattab
figures.evidence: Suspended hudud penalty for theft during famine citing public welfare considerations.

figures.name: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
figures.evidence: Policy reforms prioritized public welfare, returning confiscated properties to original owners.

figures.name: Imam Malik ibn Anas
figures.evidence: Al-Muwatta incorporates public welfare considerations in juridical reasoning alongside textual sources.

figures.name: Abu Yusuf
figures.evidence: Kitab al-Kharaj applies public welfare considerations to taxation and land policy.

figures.name: Ibn al-Qasim
figures.evidence: Transmitted Malik's consideration of public welfare in legal derivation.

figures.name: Sahnun
figures.evidence: Transmitted Maliki public welfare considerations in Al-Mudawwana's practical rulings.

figures.name: Al-Mawardi
figures.evidence: Integrated public welfare considerations into political theory in Al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyyah.

figures.name: Nizam al-Mulk
figures.evidence: Siyasatnama grounds governance in public welfare and preservation of order under shariah.

figures.name: Imam al-Juwayni
figures.evidence: Advanced public interest considerations in legal theory in al-Ghiyathi.

figures.name: Nur al-Din Zangi
figures.evidence: Promoted public welfare through hospitals, madrasas, and infrastructure projects.

figures.name: Ibn Khaldun
figures.evidence: Muqaddimah grounds governance in societal welfare through concept of asabiyyah.

figures.name: Al-Wansharisi
figures.evidence: Fatwas in al-Mi'yar frequently invoke maslaha in cases of intercommunal relations and governance.

figures.name: Al-Hajj Salim Suwari
figures.evidence: Advocated patient da'wa over jihad based on public welfare considerations.

figures.name: Ebussuud Efendi
figures.evidence: Applied public welfare considerations in fatawa addressing Ottoman state needs.

figures.name: Rifa'a at-Tahtawi
figures.evidence: Argued for adopting European sciences and institutions based on public welfare.

figures.name: Muhammad Abduh
figures.evidence: Used public welfare principle as Grand Mufti for modernizing legal rulings.

figures.name: Al-Kawakibi
figures.evidence: Invoked public welfare to justify political reforms in Arab lands against Ottoman rule.

figures.name: Qasim Amin
figures.evidence: Argued women's unveiling and education serve public welfare in modernizing Egypt.

figures.name: Tahir ibn Ashur
figures.evidence: Integrated maslaha into maqasid framework in Maqasid al-Shariah al-Islamiyya.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Qaradawi
figures.evidence: Extensively applied public welfare considerations in modern fatwa contexts across his work.

figures.name: Abdurrahman Wahid
figures.evidence: Invoked public welfare to justify inter-religious harmony and democratic governance.

figures.name: Fethullah Gulen
figures.evidence: Grounds Hizmet movement's educational and social projects in public welfare principles.

figures.name: Ziauddin Sardar
figures.evidence: Emphasized public welfare considerations in writings on Islamic futures and social reform.

concepts.definition_ar: اعتبار المنفعة العامة معياراً للأحكام حيث تسكت النصوص
concepts.definition_ur: عوامی بھلائی کو معیار بنانا جہاں نصوص خاموش ہوں

concepts.name: Al-Ahkam al-Khamsa (the five legal values)
concepts.definition: Classifying acts as obligatory, recommended, neutral, disliked, or forbidden.

figures.name: Shurayh al-Qadi
figures.evidence: Applied five-fold classification in judgments under Umar and Ali's guidance.

figures.name: Ata ibn Abi Rabah
figures.evidence: Issued legal classifications on pilgrimage rituals as Imam al-Hajj in Mecca.

figures.name: Abd al-Rahman al-Awza'i
figures.evidence: Early systematizer of legal classifications in Syrian juristic tradition before Hanafi-Shafi'i.

figures.name: Abu Dawud
figures.evidence: Structured Sunan Abu Dawud by legal categories mapping to the five-fold classification.

figures.name: Ibn Majah
figures.evidence: Sunan organized topically by legal rulings across ritual and civil matters.

figures.name: Al-Qabisi
figures.evidence: Classified legal rulings using five-value schema in educational writings.

figures.name: Al-Mawardi
figures.evidence: Applied five legal values framework throughout his juridical works.

figures.name: Al-Sarakhsi
figures.evidence: Al-Mabsut systematically categorizes acts into five legal values across all jurisprudential domains.

figures.name: Al-Qurtubi
figures.evidence: Jami' li-ahkam al-Qur'an systematically extracts legal rulings from Quranic verses.

figures.name: Yahya ibn Sharif al-Nawawi
figures.evidence: Riyad al-Salihin systematically organizes legal-ethical categories of actions.

figures.name: Al-Damiri
figures.evidence: al-Najm al-wahhāj fī sharḥ al-Minhāj is a commentary on Shafi'i legal methodology.

figures.name: Shaykh Bahai
figures.evidence: Jame-e Abbasi extensively treats Islamic ritual law and juridical classifications.

figures.name: Al-Bajuri
figures.evidence: Transmitted Shafi'i legal taxonomy in his fiqh works and teaching.

concepts.definition_ar: تصنيف الأفعال إلى واجب ومندوب ومباح ومكروه وحرام
concepts.definition_ur: افعال کی تقسیم واجب، مندوب، مباح، مکروہ اور حرام میں

concepts.name: Marja'iyya (source of emulation)
concepts.definition: Shia institution by which lay believers follow the rulings of a senior living jurist.

figures.evidence: Patronized ulama hierarchy that strengthened institutional Shia marja system in Iran.

figures.name: Hashim Larijani
figures.evidence: Held position as Grand Ayatollah and source of emulation for Shia believers.

figures.name: Ayatollah Khomeini
figures.evidence: Merged traditional marja role with political governance in founding Islamic Republic.

figures.name: Reza Zanjani

figures.name: Taqi Tabatabaei Qomi
figures.evidence: Served as marja al-taqlid with followers emulating his juristic rulings in Mashhad.

figures.name: Ahmad Azari Qomi
figures.evidence: As Qom-based cleric, participated in institution of lay believers following senior jurists.

figures.name: Yousef Madani Tabrizi
figures.evidence: As grand ayatollah served as source of emulation for Shia community in Tabriz region.

figures.name: Abbas Vaez-Tabasi
figures.evidence: Served as custodian of Imam Reza shrine, institutional role in Shia religious authority.

figures.name: Ali Mohammad Dastgheib Shirazi
figures.evidence: As Shirazi mystic in Shia context, would have operated within marja'iyya system.

figures.name: Ali Asghar Rahimi Azad
figures.evidence: As grand ayatollah, directly participated in marja institution as source of emulation.

figures.name: Ahmad Ghabel
figures.evidence: Mystic perspective likely challenged institutional clerical authority structures in Shia context.

figures.name: Hassan Khomeini
figures.evidence: Operates within Qom's marja'iyya system though not yet a marja himself.

figures.name: Muqtada al-Sadr
figures.evidence: Established alternative authority structure through Sadr movement challenging traditional hierarchy.

concepts.name: Maqamat (stations on the path)

figures.name: Harith al-Muhasibi
figures.evidence: Among first to systematize spiritual stations in structured form for Sufi path development.

figures.name: Dhul-Nun al-Misri
figures.evidence: Pioneered the systematic classification of spiritual stations in early Sufism.

figures.name: Sari al-Saqati
figures.evidence: Among first Baghdad mystics to articulate progressive spiritual stations framework.

figures.name: Junayd of Baghdad
figures.evidence: Defined and systematized the progressive spiritual stations of the Sufi path.

figures.name: Ibn Khafif
figures.evidence: Transmitted Khorasan School's systematic teaching on spiritual stations.

figures.name: Al-Sarraj al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Systematized spiritual stations in Kitab al-Luma, first encyclopedic treatment of Sufi stages.

figures.name: Abu Talib al-Makki

figures.name: Abu Nasr al-Sarraj

figures.name: Al-Sulami of Nishapur

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi

figures.name: Al-Qushayri

figures.name: Khwaja Abdullah Ansari

figures.name: Ali al-Hujwiri
figures.evidence: Kashf al-Mahjub systematizes the progressive spiritual stations of the Sufi path.

figures.name: Yusuf al-Hamadani
figures.evidence: Systematized progressive spiritual stations for disciples in Central Asian context.

figures.name: Al-Ghazali
figures.evidence: Systematized Sufi stations throughout the four quarters of Ihya Ulum al-Din.

figures.name: Abdul Qadir al-Jilani
figures.evidence: Al-Ghunya systematizes spiritual stations progressing from repentance to union.

figures.name: Abu Najib Suhrawardi

figures.name: Abdul Khaliq Ghujdawani

figures.name: Ahmad al-Rifai

figures.name: Farid ud-Din Attar

figures.name: Najm al-Din Kubra

figures.name: Shihab al-Din al-Suhrawardi

figures.name: Najm al-Din Razi

figures.name: Sharaf al-Din Maneri

figures.name: Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani

figures.name: Baha-ud-Din Naqshband

figures.name: Gesu Daraz

figures.name: Ibn Abbad al-Rundi
figures.evidence: Maps spiritual stations in his guidance letters to disciples on the Sufi path.

figures.name: Ali ibn Wafa

figures.name: Yahya al-Shirvani
figures.evidence: Systematized stations of the path for Khalwatiyya initiates following classical Sufi models.

figures.name: Ahmad Zarruq
figures.evidence: Transmitted classical Shadhili station doctrine through his Sufi writings.

figures.name: Shaykh Zarruq
figures.evidence: Detailed spiritual stations in his systematic works on Sufi path and practice.

figures.name: Bali Efendi
figures.evidence: Naqshbandi instruction involved guiding disciples through spiritual stations.

figures.name: Muhammad Ghaus Gwaliari

figures.name: Aziz Mahmud Hudayi
figures.evidence: Outlined spiritual stations in his guidance texts for disciples.

figures.name: Khwaja Baqi Billah

figures.name: Mirza Mazhar Jan-e-Janan

figures.name: Syed Ahmad Kabir Rifai

figures.name: Ashraf Ali Thanvi
figures.evidence: Detailed spiritual stations in his Sufi manuals following classical Chishti taxonomy.

concepts.name: Ahwal (spiritual states)
concepts.definition: Transient God-given conditions experienced on the path, distinct from earned stations.

figures.name: Dhul-Nun al-Misri
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient spiritual states (ahwal) from permanent stations (maqamat).

figures.name: Junayd of Baghdad
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient God-given states from stable earned stations in Sufi doctrine.

figures.name: Abu al-Husayn al-Nuri
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient states from stations under his teacher Junayd's guidance.

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Shibli
figures.evidence: Exemplified transient God-given states through his famous ecstatic episodes in Baghdad.

figures.name: Ibn Khafif
figures.evidence: Preserved distinction between stations and states in Khorasan tradition.

figures.name: Al-Sarraj al-Tusi
figures.evidence: Distinguished transient states from stations in Kitab al-Luma, foundational for later Sufism.

figures.name: Abu Talib al-Makki
figures.evidence: Qut al-Qulub distinguishes transient spiritual states from earned stations.

figures.name: Abu Nasr al-Sarraj

figures.name: Al-Sulami of Nishapur

figures.name: Abu Bakr al-Kalabadhi

figures.name: Al-Tawhidi

figures.name: Al-Sulami of Nishapur

figures.name: Dawud al-Kayseri

concepts.name: Ilm al-Hay'a (mathematical cosmography)

figures.evidence: Commissioned astronomical observations and Ptolemaic works translated at Baghdad observatory.

figures.name: Abu Ma'shar al-Balkhi

figures.name: Al-Farghani
figures.evidence: Kitab fi Jawami Ilm al-Nujum systematized Ptolemaic cosmography for Arabic audiences.

figures.name: Al-Biruni

figures.name: Imam Muslim

figures.name: Al-Baghawi

figures.name: Al-Qadi Iyad

figures.name: Shuhda al-Katiba
